title: Rabbi Hillel son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Berakhot 28b, saying that the Eighteen Benedictions were instituted to correspond to the eighteen mentions of God’s name that David said in “Ascribe to the Lord, O sons of the mighty.” In Shabbat 80a: “Hillel son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani (supplied דרשב״ג) interpreted.” Hyman also cites Sheviit, beginning of chapter 6; Kiddushin 1:8; Shir HaShirim Rabbah 8:10; and Kohelet Rabbah 1:4.

notes.text: The supplied דרשב״ג remains a genuine letter/abbreviation question, even though the connected statement about Shmuel bar Nachmani’s father is translated. No silent replacement of those letters or printed-pixel confirmation is claimed.

The supplied Shabbat abbreviation is דרשב״ג, retained explicitly in the translation. The heading and the saved Davidson Shabbat 80a text name Hillel as the son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani, supporting that contextual rendering rather than Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. The question concerns Hillel’s father, not Shmuel bar Nachmani’s father. Whether the supplied ג reflects Hyman’s printed page or a transcription difference remains unresolved; no printed-pixel or letter-history verification is claimed.

The printed Hyman page (vol. I, p. 375) reads דרשב״נ ending in the letter nun. The supplied transcription, retained above, has דרשב״ג. The consulted Shabbat 80a and Berakhot 28b explicitly name Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani as Hillel’s father. The parallel on Nehemiah 8:17 in the Jerusalem Talmud, Sheviit 6:1 and Kiddushin 1:8, and in Kohelet Rabbah 1:4 uses Shmuel bar Nachman. Hillel’s saying on the teacher and student is at Shir HaShirim Rabbah 8:11 in the consulted digital edition, on biblical Song of Songs 8:12. Hyman’s reference is 8:10.
